title: Halcyon Drift Rising Revisited
premise: Elodie Winterbourne, a terraformer tending a garden meant for people not yet born, runs the long route between two fleets that no longer speak, carrying seed stock and silence in equal measure. When an unfamiliar name appears on the manifest of a ship that never flew — a vessel erased from every record — he is pulled into a conspiracy spanning both fleets: the war that severed them was manufactured to hide Earth's final transmission loop, which is quietly running out. To keep the lie alive that holds the fleets apart from open slaughter, Elodie must impersonate the dead man on the manifest, becoming the bridge neither side will build for itself. In the end he chooses truth over peace-keeping deception, broadcasting the loop's last message as both fleets converge — and the found family he assembled along the drift carries his garden's seeds toward a world where memory can finally take root.
about_author: Dominic Dunmore is the pen name of a former orbital hydroponics engineer who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. He lives somewhere with unreliable gravity and writes about the people who keep impossible systems running.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Elodie tends the generation-ship arboretum on Halcyon Drift, speaking aloud to children who may never be born. POV: Elodie. Establishes his loneliness and devotion; ends when a manifest update flags a name — Cassian Vey — on a ship decommissioned before it ever launched.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghost
chapters.summary: Elodie investigates the impossible entry, finding the Meridian logged as never-flown yet scheduled for departure. POV: Elodie. Curiosity curdles into unease as dock records show the ship crewed by people who officially don't exist.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Loading run between the Halcyon fleet and the rival Ashfall convoy; Elodie smuggles nothing but notices others do. POV: Elodie. Introduces the cold truce between fleets and his role as trusted neutral courier.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Counts Seeds
chapters.summary: Meet Ilsa Reyes, Halcyon's quartermaster, who audits Elodie's garden and suspects the manifest anomaly is deliberate bait. POV: Ilsa. Wary alliance forms; she warns him some names are traps set by fleet intelligence.

chapters.title: Ashfall Welcome
chapters.summary: Elodie docks at Ashfall Prime, greeted by Commander Dae-Sun Okonkwo, who asks pointed questions about the Meridian. POV: Elodie. Tension: Ashfall knows something about the ghost ship and wants him to find it first.

chapters.title: A Name He Never Chose
chapters.summary: Someone calls Elodie 'Cassian' in a crowded market — and believes it. POV: Elodie. Uncanny beat: facial recognition across both fleets insists he matches a man dead eleven years.

chapters.title: The Loop
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals Earth's last transmission loop: a dying broadcast repeating humanity's final message, its power failing within months. POV: Ilsa. The stakes crystallize — both fleets were built around escaping what that message describes.

chapters.title: Meridian Rising
chapters.summary: Elodie boards the never-flown Meridian at night; its corridors are lived-in, warm, wrong. POV: Elodie. Dread builds as he finds personal effects — including a photograph of himself, younger, smiling.

chapters.title: Cassian Vey's Log
chapters.summary: Recovered logs show Cassian Vey discovered the loop was falsified — Earth's message edited by fleet founders to justify the separation. POV: Cassian (flashback). Tragic counterpoint: Vey was silenced before he could tell anyone.

chapters.title: Family of Strangers
chapters.summary: The Meridian's hidden crew — engineers, archivists, a child named Pip — reveal themselves; they've waited years for someone wearing Vey's face. POV: Elodie. Found family begins forming under false pretenses he can't yet confess.

chapters.title: What the Fleets Remember
chapters.summary: Dual timeline: how Halcyon and Ashfall split after the 'Betrayal Broadcast.' POV: Archivist Nour Haddad. Historical chapter reframing the war as theater maintained by both leaderships.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: A Halcyon patrol boards the Meridian; Elodie must pass as Vey to save the hidden crew. POV: Elodie. First lie told under pressure — and it works, which frightens him more than failure would.

chapters.title: Pip's Stars
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude: Pip, born aboard the ghost ship, teaches Elodie her invented constellations. POV: Pip. Tender beat cementing the found family; Elodie almost tells the truth about who he is.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Offer
chapters.summary: Dae-Sun offers Elodie command of an Ashfall retrieval mission targeting the transmission array. POV: Dae-Sun. Moral pressure: accepting means betraying Halcyon; refusing means losing access to the truth.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Ilsa confronts Elodie: fleet high commands know the loop is failing and are using the countdown to force unification — or annihilation. POV: Ilsa. Revelation that the 'peace' is a hostage situation built on his double identity.

chapters.title: Signal Decay
chapters.summary: Technical crisis: the loop's degradation accelerates; forty days remain. POV: Engineer Tomas Beck. Countdown established; both fleets mobilize toward the relay station, each believing the other will seize it.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Airlock
chapters.summary: Sabotage strikes the Meridian; a crew member dies protecting the archives. POV: Elodie. Grief and guilt — the lie he keeps alive now has a body count.

chapters.title: Confession at the Garden
chapters.summary: Elodie tells Ilsa everything: the face, the logs, the hidden crew. POV: Elodie. Vulnerable midpoint turn; instead of betrayal, she chooses to help him become Vey fully — or bury him honestly.

chapters.title: The Second Face
chapters.summary: Nour reconstructs Vey's final days: he wasn't murdered but chose erasure, seeding his identity as a future key. POV: Nour. Reframe: Elodie isn't an impostor; he's an inheritance.

chapters.title: Convoy Shadow
chapters.summary: Ashfall warships shadow the Meridian; Dae-Sun transmits an ultimatum disguised as an invitation. POV: Dae-Sun. Antagonist depth — he genuinely believes seizing the loop will save more lives than truth will.

chapters.title: Forty Days
chapters.summary: Fleet councils convene separately; both vote to move on the relay. POV: Councilor Amara Voss (Halcyon). Political machinery grinds toward collision while Elodie's window narrows.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Elodie runs his old courier route one last time, carrying messages between fleets as himself, not Vey. POV: Elodie. Bittersweet farewell tour; each stop, someone trusts him with something true.

chapters.title: Pip's Question
chapters.summary: Pip asks if Elodie is Cassian; he answers honestly for the first time. POV: Pip. Emotional keystone — she decides he's family anyway, redefining identity as chosen rather than given.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Ashfall forces board mid-route; Elodie is taken to Dae-Sun, who reveals he knows Elodie isn't Vey — and doesn't care. POV: Elodie. Captivity arc opens; Dae-Sun needs a living symbol more than a truthful man.

chapters.title: The Puppet Fleet
chapters.summary: Dae-Sun plans to parade 'Cassian Vey returned' before both fleets to legitimize Ashfall's claim on the relay. POV: Dae-Sun. Villain logic laid bare: a useful lie beats a costly truth.

chapters.title: Escape Velocity
chapters.summary: Ilsa and the Meridian crew mount a rescue using the ghost ship's phantom registry to spoof Ashfall sensors. POV: Tomas Beck. Action beat; the ship that never flew finally flies, carrying its stolen family out.

chapters.title: Broken Transmission
chapters.summary: They reach the relay early — and find it already occupied by a third party: descendants of Earth's original broadcast team, alive all along. POV: Elodie. Twist: the loop's keepers have been waiting for someone to come listen.

chapters.title: The Unedited Message
chapters.summary: The keepers play Earth's true final transmission: not a warning, but an apology and an invitation home. POV: Elodie. Devastating hope — the war's foundation dissolves, but so does the lie keeping the fleets from open battle.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Silence
chapters.summary: Both armadas arrive at the relay; commanders demand the loop for themselves. POV: Amara Voss. Standoff chapter; Elodie realizes releasing the truth could trigger the very war it was meant to prevent.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Elodie weighs Dae-Sun's final offer: maintain the founding lie forever, with him as its eternal face, and everyone lives in comfortable falsehood. POV: Elodie. Dark night of the soul; the garden metaphor returns — seeds need truth to grow.

chapters.title: Broadcast Day
chapters.summary: Elodie hijacks the loop's final hours, splicing the unedited message into both fleets' channels. POV: Elodie. Climax begins: the truth goes out, unstoppable, as weapons arm on both sides.

chapters.title: What Cassian Would Do
chapters.summary: Chaos at the relay; Dae-Sun moves to destroy the transmitter, and Elodie physically stands between. POV: Elodie. Climactic confrontation — he speaks as both himself and Vey, offering the fleets a shared inheritance instead of a shared enemy.

chapters.title: Ceasefire in the Static
chapters.summary: As the true message plays fleet-wide, soldiers lower weapons; Dae-Sun, confronted by his own crew's grief, stands down. POV: Dae-Sun. Climax resolves through witnessed truth, not victory — the antagonist is undone by empathy he can't order away.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: The loop ends, its final words delivered; both fleets drift in shared silence, then begin talking. POV: Ilsa. Exhausted, fragile hope; negotiations begin with the keepers as neutral ground.

chapters.title: Burial for a Borrowed Name
chapters.summary: Elodie formally retires Cassian Vey's identity, holding a funeral attended by both fleets. POV: Elodie. Catharsis — grief for a man he never was, gratitude for the life the name made possible.

chapters.title: Seeds for Two Worlds
chapters.summary: The garden's seed stock is divided: half to Halcyon, half to Ashfall, with the keepers' archive as common ground. POV: Pip. Generational beat — the garden for the unborn becomes gardens for the born.

chapters.title: The Joint Route
chapters.summary: First joint courier mission between the fleets; old enemies share a cockpit. POV: Tomas Beck. Reconciliation in small gestures; the long route between worlds that no longer speak finds its voice again.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Revised
chapters.summary: Both fleets vote on a course: not back to a dead Earth, but toward the world the original message described — a place prepared long ago. POV: Amara Voss. Collective decision replaces inherited division.

chapters.title: The Last Manifest
chapters.summary: Elodie files the Meridian's first honest flight plan, listing every crew member by their real names. POV: Elodie. Quiet resolution — the ship that never flew is finally, truly flown.

chapters.title: Halcyon Drift Rising
chapters.summary: Years later, Elodie plants the final bed in a new world's soil, Pip beside him, both fleets' children learning the same constellations. POV: Elodie. Closing echo of chapter one: the garden was always for the living; memory kept them, and truth set them down.
